meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'легал'). Common masculine noun meaning 'illegal immigrant' in everyday Russian.
Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('Good Lord!') used directly in spoken exchanges.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'where'.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to put'.

examples.text: Куда ты вечно деваешь чистые полотенца со моего стола?
examples.trans: Where do you always put the clean towels from my table?

examples.text: На складе так много коробок, что их уже просто некуда девать.
examples.trans: There are so many boxes in the stockroom that there is simply nowhere to put them anymore.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'сидеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sit out'.

examples.trans: You will sit in the toilet.

examples.text: Во время проверки вам придётся тихо отсидеться в кабинете.
examples.trans: During the inspection you will have to quietly sit it out in the office.

examples.text: Никому не удастся спокойно отсидеться в стороне во время банкета.
examples.trans: No one will manage to quietly sit on the sidelines during the banquet.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'toilet', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The toilet is in the corridor.
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (on foot)', paired with 'уходить'.
+ accusative: через неделю = in a week
Secondary conversational sense ('through, across') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'entrance', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: There at the cemetery is the main entrance.
Where is the entrance to the metro?
We will open this entrance right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('they') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be on duty'.

examples.trans: They are on guard at the entrance.

examples.text: Они сегодня весь вечер дежурят на входе.
examples.trans: They are on duty at the entrance all evening today.

examples.text: Кто из поваров будет дежурить на кухне в субботу?
examples.trans: Which of the cooks will be on duty in the kitchen on Saturday?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to sit down, to take a seat
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'есть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sit down', paired with 'садиться'.

examples.trans: He sat down on a chair.
Listen, sit down. Sit down, please.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hall', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('living room') (regional/colloquial) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.en: to go and come back, to pop over
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ходить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'ходить'.

examples.trans: Yes, go on. Don't mix it up with another one!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar, pub' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.
It is already morning. Our bar is closing.

meanings.note: singular in Russian, unlike English

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

терпеть.gloss: to bear, to put up with; to hold on

meanings.en: to put up with, to bear
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to bear', forming an aspectual pair with 'потерпеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to hold on, to wait') (e.g. to wait for the toilet) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Маленькие умеют терпеть, а взрослые нет, понял?
examples.trans: Little ones can hold on, but grown-ups can't, got it?

related.gloss: to be patient for a while

давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здравлять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to congratulate', forming an aspectual pair with 'поздравить'.

Secondary conversational sense ('pure') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нин, я всё помыл. Всё чисто.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'right', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Go on, tell her. Nina doesn't believe it.
